answer: A mechanism that actually bites: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because echo only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, mesa is enforced in the ledger: Every gate is public and recomputable, so honest agents can verify they were treated fairly. Any spiral approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
